b.notes:
1. The biggest usability gain this round is plain. Every refinement and graft brought the count of targets under 44px to 0 on every page, against 7 to 23 on the carried designs and their mutants. That alone lifts each lineage by about two points through this lens. All three dice mutants inherit their parents' small targets and caps, and none of their rolls (cyanotype, full glow, Azeret) changes how a page is used.

2. Each lineage now leads with a different interaction strength:
- Figure Ground: joining a figure to the list it draws (To do's NOW line across the rows, Ideas' kind figure as the filter, Status's summary numbers as links).
- Flight Console: saying state in words next to the light (the WORKING and OFF windows), and matching numbered stops to numbered rows.
- Switchboard: one rack repeated on every page, with the primary always in the same place. Of all the ideas, this is the most standard-worthy system for To do, Ideas, Plans and Settings.

3. Grafted features that worked:
- Round tubes in the page heads, and the hover-lit figure marks (figure-graft).
- The Status meter and pilot jewels (console-graft).
- The row of page keys with numbers, icons and a lit LED for 'here' (switchboard-graft).
- Segmented Show keys in place of a select (console lineage).

4. Grafted features that did not work:
- Per-row T-minus ladders, which repeat 'in N days' in code.
- Mosaic pictures, which do not read as data.
- Moving 'ways to start' away from the box.
- An unlabelled grid of lamp dots on Status.
- Fig. numbering as costume.

5. Keyboard: Flight Console puts six readout links before the box in Tab order, and on the phone the box falls below the fold. That is the one thing keeping console-refine off first place.

6. Compared with the yardsticks, figure-refine and console-refine both beat Desk Terminal, Joined (7.5) on how clearly a page says its state, and everything except the mutants beats today's page (5).

scores.why: Yardstick. The hierarchy is plain and clear: greeting, box, Send, then the lists. But Home has 43 of 56 targets under 44px (To do 46 of 97), the chips are small, and blurred it reads as one green-lit card over a flat list. The title says nothing about the job.

Yardstick. No target under 44px on any page, a compact 1480px Home, and numbered sections that read in order. The question sits on the glass above the field. The NOW line crossing To do is a strong cue. The FROM/Send block is split below the glass, and the section numbers carry little.

The figure-per-section structure is readable. But it has 14 small targets on Home and 20 on To do, a nav of tracked mono capitals ('01 HOME'), every row title underlined as a blue link (noisy to scan), and a 2437px Home.

The best sight line in the heat: title, box, then Send in one lit pool, with the textarea straight after the nav in Tab order and no target under 44px anywhere. Its To do NOW line runs across the list itself, so late sits above it and due below, which you get in one glance. Status's '3 of 4 answering / 1 of 4 key set / $0.00 of $2.00' are links, and Ideas' kind figure doubles as the kind filter. On the phone the title and box come first.

The full-width tables on a 24px rhythm are very easy to scan. A round tube in each page head ('2 LATE' on To do) is read instantly, and hovering a row lights its mark in the figure. Each caption says in words what its figure shows. Against it: an empty band under the Status and Chat heads, chat arrows that miss their lines, and a phone Home whose first screen does not say what is next.

It keeps all of the parent's usability faults: 14 small targets, a 2459px Home, and caps (now small caps) on the nav and buttons. Every row title is now bright cyan and underlined, which makes the lists harder to scan than the parent's. The rounded tubes add light but no understanding.

The flight plan and crew board are good ideas for taking things in at a glance. But it has 23 small targets on Home, a nav of tracked-capital text, 'HOLDS' and T-minus words the family has to decode, the readout says things the page says again, and the setup ladder is costume.

The clearest state language in the heat. Status windows say WORKING or OFF in words beside the lamp. The flight plan's numbered rings match the numbered rows, so 'when' and 'what' join up. Against it: the six readout stops come before the box in Tab order, and on the phone the box falls below the readout and the monitor.

Against it: the per-plan T-minus ladders repeat 'in 4 days' in a code the family has to learn, To do's add action is only a disclosure row with no visible primary, and 'Tell Vera what's next.' is narrower than the job.

The lit readout windows do make the figures pop in the squint. But the parent's faults are all still there: 23 small targets on Home, a nav of tracked capitals, T-minus and HOLDS costume, and a 2229px Home. More glow is not more understanding.

The sommaire map is a real way-finding idea, with every page, its count and its lamp in one view. But it has 7 small targets, cut-off plan names ('Mount St. Helens da…'), an empty Memory cell, tracked-capital keys ('+ ADD AN IDEA'), and page numbers that mean nothing to the family.

The most learnable system here. That makes To do and Ideas the quickest pages in the heat to use. Against it: 'ways to start' moved to a separate Vera cell away from the box, which breaks the sight line. The mosaic pictures do not read as data. b.titles: The best is 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (t1-figure-refine). As a label it says who hears you and what the box is for, it names the planner's whole job, it fits one line on a phone, and the lit word 'plan' is the right key word. The close second is 'What's the plan?' (t1-figure-graft, t1-console-refine, t1-switchboard-refine, t1-switchboard-graft). It is the shortest and most natural family phrase, and it works both as a question to put to Vera and as an invitation to tell her one, which suits a box that takes both kinds of message. It is at its best typed on the glass in the switchboard, where it reads as the machine's prompt. It does not name Vera, but her name sits just above it on every design. 'Tell Vera what's next.' (t1-console-graft) is the weakest new title: 'next' leaves out ideas kept for someday, the wish lists and memory, and it echoes the Next up screen beside it instead of the box's job. The mutants keep 'What's on your mind?', which fails as before because it does not say what the app is for. Recommendation: make 'Tell Vera what to plan.' the standard label, and keep 'What's the plan?' for the terminal-style glass where a prompt reads better than an instruction.

b.notes: What worked across the heat, typographically. The Plex superfamily (Sans or Sans Condensed for heads, Sans for reading, Mono for figures and times, VT323 only on the glass) is the right pairing, and every lineage now uses it. The refinements' biggest gain was dropping tracked mono caps from the bar and controls: console-refine and figure-refine read far calmer than their parents because of it. Four devices are worth making standard: dotted leaders from name to fact (switchboard-refine everywhere, console-refine in Coming up), two-line dates with the relative word in sans over the absolute date in mono (console-refine To do), run-in bold actions in lists of steps (figure-refine setup), and stat blocks with a big numeral, a small unit and a label (figure-refine Status). Two standing faults remain in most designs: 12px tracked mono caps for eyebrows, kind words and column heads, and zero-padded readouts (console lineage). On grafts: figure-graft's sentence-case kinds and its 24px baseline worked well, but the round tubes brought VT323 back at sizes too small to read. Console-graft's compact, content-sized rail worked; its title did not. Switchboard-graft's sentence-case labels and bold run-in figures worked, but dropping the leader dots cost the lineage its typographic signature. Of the mutants, figure-mut's small caps are the right instinct in the wrong face, switchboard-mut's Azeret Mono is nearly invisible (and its slashed zero reads as code in prose counts), and console-mut's VT323 windows make figures harder to read. Against the yardsticks: figure-refine and switchboard-refine now match or pass Desk Terminal, Joined on typesetting, and every refine is well ahead of today's page.

scores.why: Yardstick. A geometric sans with small, same-weight headings: 'Coming up' and 'To do' are barely bigger than the body. To do shows ISO dates ('Due 2026-09-27 19:56') and pills. Nothing is set to a scale or a grid, and hierarchy comes from boxes, not type.

Yardstick. The Plex superfamily with real scale tokens (--fs-page/title/head/text/note), numbered section heads, tabular times and a VT323 title in the tube. Two things hold it back: relative words like 'in 4 days' and 'was due 3 days ago' are set in mono, and the left column is crowded with small text.

The large Plex Condensed display heads give the page its strongest hierarchy. Against that: 12px tracked mono caps are everywhere (the '01 HOME' bar, 'CHAPTER 3', '[IN 4 DAYS]'), row titles are blue underlined links, and To do shows ISO dates ('Due 2026-09-27 19:56').

The best reading typography in the heat. The condensed display heads are well scaled (page title, then plate head, then row). Setup steps have run-in bold actions ('Choose your own password, so everybody…'). Status figures are set as '3 of 4' with a small unit and a label. Dates are tabular mono ('Sun 4 Oct', '13:00'), measures sit at 58–62ch, and Fig. captions are consistent. On To do the NOW rule runs through the list itself. What remains is the 12px tracked mono caps on kind words and eyebrows, and some straight apostrophes.

The most rigorous vertical rhythm here: every plate sits on a 24px line, rows are 48px, and 'Fig. n.n' captions hang with their text aligned. Kinds are now sentence case and the date column has a bold day numeral ('Thu 1 Oct'). It loses points for three things: the Ideas list merges distance and 'for' into one right-aligned ragged run, so the figures don't line up; the VT323 inside the small round tubes ('10:00 TOMORROW') is too small; and there is a dark empty band under the title-only heads.

Moving labels to small caps instead of shouted capitals is a sound typographic instinct. But it brings in a fourth face (Barlow Condensed), fakes the small-cap figures, and still sets the bar and buttons in caps. The cyan links and the ISO dates on To do are unchanged.

The readout strip has a nice console voice, but the text is mostly 11–12px tracked mono caps: the bar, 'CONSOLE 03 | TARGETS OF OPPORTUNITY' and the 'FIG. 1' captions. Figures are zero-padded, and the small captions and chat call signs are hard to read.

This refinement makes a real typographic cleanup. The bar and labels are sentence case, and the readout rail pairs small semibold sans labels with mono figures. Coming up uses dotted leaders with bold mono times. Due dates are set in two lines, the relative 'Was due 3 days ago' in sans over the absolute 'Sun 27 Sep, 19:56' in mono, which is the best date pairing in the heat. The remaining costume is the zero-padding ('04', 'Needs a look 00', 'Free weekends 00 of 01'). The rail cells are too wide for their figures, and the setup links wrap in narrow columns.

It shares the refine's sentence-case system. The rail is more compact and sized to its content, and Status sets '3 of 4 on' with running text that bolds its figures ('$0.00 of the $2.00'). But the page reads more fragmented, with cards and lamp columns, the zero-padding stays, and the title 'Tell Vera what’s next.' is weaker wording.
Putting every rail figure in a small blurred VT323 window lowers legibility with no gain in hierarchy. The parent's tracked mono caps bar, 'CONSOLE nn' eyebrows and zero-padded readouts all stay.

The contents-line idea is inherently typographic (number, name, leader, count). Against it: the family's placeholder is set in VT323, the keys are tracked caps ('+ ADD AN IDEA'), there are many mono caps eyebrows, and the cells stretch half-empty, which breaks the rhythm.

This is a complete type system. Every page runs the same leader-dot register (name, dots, facts), with right-aligned tabular drive times and the compass as its own column ('2h 45 min W'). The family's words are in a Plex well, and the VT323 title gets a hand-fitted Plex curly apostrophe. Counts and page numbers stay quiet. Still to fix: the tracked mono caps eyebrows and column heads ('AFTER NEXT UP', 'SHOW', 'KIND', '# TO DO'), and the stacked 'OPEN / 2 late' beside the To do title.

b.titles: The best is "What’s the plan?" (figure-graft, console-refine, both switchboard designs). It is the family's own phrase and names the whole job in one word. It fits one line at 2–2.9rem on a phone, and its one lit word, "plan", is a noun that holds up at any size, even in VT323 on the glass, where switchboard-refine's hand-fitted curly apostrophe sets it best. A close second is "Tell Vera what to plan." (figure-refine). It uses the manual's imperative voice, names Vera, and is plainly an invitation to tell her something; the full stop gives it a calm, set feel. It is slightly narrower, since a reminder or a wish is not something one "plans". "Tell Vera what’s next." (console-graft) is weaker. "Next" repeats the NEXT UP monitor just above it, and ideas and wishes are not "next", so it reads more like asking the app than telling it. "What comes next?" (left over in switchboard-graft's _ask.html) has the same problem. "What’s on your mind?" (r10, r11, r12 and every mutant) fails the job, as the owner said. One typesetting note: switchboard-graft sets "What's" with a straight tick to dodge VT323's quote glyph, when the refine's Plex-apostrophe span solves the same problem correctly.

b.notes: On the owner's test: all three refinements change the page content itself. Figure-refine lays the lists beside their drawings, console-refine adds a readout rail and worded annunciator windows, and switchboard-refine turns Home into a directory and every other page into a module beside a register. None is a wash, and each makes a task easier. The dice mutants barely change the pages, and for use they are worse than or equal to their parents: console-mut's full-strength tubes put the most glare on the radar, not the box; figure-mut's small caps put capitals on every button. Phosphor through this lens: a design uses light well when the brightest things are the primary, focus and the live mark. Figure-refine and console-refine do that; the switchboard's big lit glass on Home makes the monitor, not the box, the brightest thing at night (64% green share). Grafted features that worked: figure-graft's one-line to-do rows and the next plan as a lit row at the top of Coming up; console-graft's Status meter with a plain sentence beside it and its amber 'This page' row, an action an admin can take; switchboard-graft's large labelled page keys (0 small targets) and its '4 open · 2 late' heading. Grafts that did not work: console-graft's T-minus ladders and four-shape lamp code, codes a family must learn for facts the words already give; switchboard-graft's mosaic pictograms and unlabeled status dots, which look like data but cannot be read; its numbered select options; Settings pulled out of the tab row and first in Tab order; figure-graft's decorative Figs 1.4 and 1.5 and its numbered nav. Tab order: figure-refine and figure-graft reach the textarea straight after the nav. Console-refine and console-graft put six rail links first. Switchboard-refine puts three links first, and switchboard-graft puts Settings before Home. Every refinement and graft reached 0 targets under 44px; the carried designs and mutants did not (r10/figure-mut 14, r11/console-mut 23, r12/switchboard-mut 7). Across lineages, three things are worth carrying forward: figure-refine's NOW line drawn across the list, console-refine's rail figures as links to the filtered list, and switchboard-refine's Settings directory on Home with the part that needs a look flagged.

scores.why: Yardstick. It is familiar and the box is easy to find, but Home has 43 of 56 targets under 44px, To do is below the fold and shows ISO dates ('Due 2026-09-27 19:56'), each to-do's actions hide in a disclosure, and the text goes down to 11.5px.

Yardstick. No small targets, a numbered Home that reads at a glance, NOW drawn across the To do list, Ideas as one scannable table with kind keys, and a Status meter. But the Next up links come before the box in Tab order, and the title and placeholder sit in VT323 on the glass.

The box comes first and the figures carry real data. But the nav is tracked mono caps ('01 HOME'), 14 Home targets are under 44px, row titles are underlined blue like raw links, To do repeats ISO due dates with LATE chips, Home runs 2448px, and the phone tab bar is text only.

The best path to the main task. The textarea is the first Tab stop after the nav, and 'Tell Vera what to plan.' sits directly over it, one line on the phone too. Coming up and To do sit side by side above the fold. On To do, a lit NOW line crosses the list between the late and the upcoming items, so what is overdue reads at once. It has 0 small targets and sentence-case keys. What holds it back: Ideas' kind filter lives only in the drawing (the Kind select is gone from the filter row), '#4' ids compete with task titles, and Home's vertical four-week figure is hard to read.

Very readable: each to-do is one line (title, who, due), the next plan is the first Coming up row with its lamp, and there are 0 small targets. The box comes straight after the nav in Tab order. But Home is 1779px, Figs 1.4 and 1.5 (rungs, squares) say nothing the lists don't while using a 280px column on every plate, the nav carries '01 02' numbers, and on the phone the next plan falls below the first screen.

It keeps all the parent's faults: 14 small targets, ISO dates, 'Chapter'/'Fig.' costume, a 2448px Home. It adds small caps on every button ('SEND', 'FILTER', 'SKIP TO THE PAGE'), which are still capitals to read, and turns the underlined row links a brighter cyan, which makes the raw-link look worse.

The readout strip is a real at-a-glance gain. But there are 23 small targets on Home, the nav is tracked mono caps, the Status annunciator is a wall of tiny capital windows that repeats the lists below it, and Home runs 2229px with Coming up below a flight plan the family must decode.

State is the clearest in the heat. The rail figures are links, so 'Late 02' is one click to the late list. Status windows say WORKING or OFF in words. To do has one-click Show keys and an Edit button on each row. The title sits inside the box's border, so it is plainly the box's label. The costs: zero-padded figures (05, 04, 00), six rail stops before the textarea in Tab order, a pushed-down box on the phone, lamp legends to learn on To do, and a Plans track whose past band is on another scale.

The Status meter with a plain sentence beside it, and the amber 'This page' row that tells an admin what to do, are real gains, and there are 0 small targets. But the T-minus ladders beside each plan and the setup ladder are unlabeled codes. To do puts a lamp column beside the checkbox, so each row has two left-edge marks. The rail also comes before the box in Tab order.

It is the parent with its tubes at full strength: 46% of the colour is green, and the brightest things on Home and Ideas are the radars, not the box. That is more glare for tired eyes, and none of the parent's faults are fixed (23 small targets, tracked caps, zero padding, a 2229px Home).

Home as the map of every page is a real way to find things. But Home has no row of page keys, so the nav differs from every other page. It keeps tracked-caps keys ('ADD AN IDEA', 'SEND'), 7 small targets, half-empty cells, and a box whose typed words and placeholder are VT323 on the glass. The Next up links come before the box in Tab order.

The best way around the whole app. Every Home cell gives a count and its first rows as links. The Settings cell lists every part and flags the one that needs a look. Ideas is a register of all 12 ideas with one-click kind keys (Restaurant). To do is a register with Edit, and the phone chat docks its composer. Nav and 'here' are the same on every page. The costs: page numbers (200, 990, 998) are noise to a family, and the composer is split, with the well inside the glass and From/Send below it. Boxed digits mean both setup steps and prompt chips, and three stops come before the textarea.

The full-width tab row has big labelled keys. But Settings sits alone in the top bar and comes first in Tab order, before Home. The mosaic pictograms (bulb, clipboard, gift, figures) and Status's 'every line at a glance' dots look like data but cannot be read. Kind is a select again, select options carry '01 02' numbers, and the phone Tab order leaves the visual order.

This is typesetting only. The slashed zero and balanced headings help a little with reading codes and titles. But every fault of the parent stays: no page keys on Home, tracked-caps keys, 7 small targets, half-empty cells, and VT323 in the box.

fixes.suggestion: KEEP: the textarea as the first Tab stop, with 'Tell Vera what to plan.' as its <label>. b.titles: Best: 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (t1-figure-refine) and 'What’s the plan?' (t1-figure-graft, t1-console-refine, t1-switchboard-refine, t1-switchboard-graft). 'Tell Vera what to plan.' is the clearest for a first-time user. It is an instruction that says who you are talking to and what for, so nobody wonders what the box is. It fits one line on a 390px phone, and 'plan' is the one lit word. 'What’s the plan?' is the family's own idiom and the shortest; it covers weekends, the calendar and reminders alike. It works best where it plainly labels the box: console-refine sets it inside the box's border, which is the best placement in the heat. In the switchboard glass it sits under the Next up monitor, split from it only by a dashed rule, and can read as that monitor's heading rather than the label of the well below. Switchboard-graft's straight apostrophe in VT323 is fine. Weaker: 'Tell Vera what’s next.' (t1-console-graft). 'Next' narrows the job to the immediate, when ideas to keep someday, wishes and a March birthday are not 'next'. It can also be parsed as a request to Vera ('Tell [me], Vera, what’s next'). Fails: 'What’s on your mind?' (r10-wild-4, r11-wild-3, r12-wmut-1 and all three mutants). It is generic and says nothing about planning, so a first-time user gets no hint of what Vera does.

b.notes: Skeptic's summary: the three refinements are the real contenders and genuinely differ from each other, which the dice mutants do not. All three mutants (figure-mut, console-mut, switchboard-mut) are near-duplicates of their parents at viewing size, and each keeps or worsens its parent's standing fault: cyan links, more glow over tracked-cap costume, and an invisible font change. console-mut shows that more glow alone moves back toward the Matrix: the whole rail lights, not just what is live. The refinements answer the owner's latest word: the content itself changed (a rail and keyed flight plan, a service map, figures joined to lists). Each still under-delivers one thing. Console lacks returned phosphor. Switchboard lacks variety and its inner pages drift toward the leader; its hue entropy of 0.436 is the lowest of the new entrants. Figure lacks consistency: Plans has no figure and Home's figure is cryptic. Grafts that worked: console-graft's moving-coil meter (an instrument on a live number, the right place for tube light); switchboard-graft's To do table and Vera cell on Home; figure-graft's one-line row typography and its Plans 'NEXT IN 1 DAY' tube. Grafts that failed: figure-graft's amber phosphor tubes (a warning costume, and neon amber against 'grounded elsewhere'); console-graft's ladders (they read as signal or battery bars); switchboard-graft's mosaics (confetti, not data), its doubled navigation and its unlabelled lamp grid. Yardsticks: Desk Terminal (7) is still the steadiest whole, but console-refine and switchboard-refine match or beat it on the owner's 'reflect the page content' test, and figure-refine's NOW line through To do is an idea the leader does not have. Today's page (3) remains the green wash the tournament set out to fix.

scores.why: Yardstick. The green wash over the greeting, pill chips, the orange initials and amber setup box read as a generic dark template with a Matrix tint. The phosphor is everywhere, so nothing stands out as lit.

Yardstick. A coherent, calm system with its phosphor in the right places (the terminal, the meter, the TO DO glass). But the steel-blue neutrals lean toward an editor theme, and the same left module on every page makes the pages look alike.

The idea is strong, but the faults are the ones the tour set out to fix: tracked mono caps in the bar ('01 HOME'), blue underlined row titles that look like raw HTML links, 'Chapter n'/'Fig. n.n' costume, a paper-grey 'here' block and small cryptic figures.

The best single idea in the heat: To do's NOW line runs out of the figure and across the list, so figure and page content become one. The lit live wire on Status works, the typesetting is quiet and good, and the title is strong. Against it: Plans has no figure (the lineage rule breaks), Home's Fig. 1 needs a four-symbol legend to decode, the chat has almost no phosphor, and the kinds are still tracked mono caps.

Calm, well-set rows, and the round tube in each page head is a real idea. But the To do and Settings tubes glow neon amber, which reads as a warning lamp and breaks 'grounded elsewhere'. Home's setup-rungs and 'a square per idea' figures only repeat their lists, the '01 Home' numbering stays, and the left gutter is mostly empty graph paper.
Nearly identical to its parent. The cyan turn makes the raw-link fault brighter, the small caps are still caps, and Barlow adds a fourth face. The rounded tubes are the only visible change.
A good skeleton (readout rail, flight plan, annunciator) under costume: tracked caps with dots in the bar, 'CONSOLE 03 · TARGETS OF OPPORTUNITY', T-minus, and tiny tracked-cap windows on Status.

The most complete system in the heat. Every page opens on a readout rail. The flight plan is drawn once and keyed to numbered rows on Home and Plans. The annunciator windows are Status's own column, violet only draws lines and amber has one job, so the page content changed, not a corner. Faults: zero-padded costume ('05', 'Free weekends 00 of 01'), counts said twice (rail Late 02 and '2 late'), a small Next up tube and a weak ask pool, so the phosphor is under-returned.

Almost a duplicate of the refinement on Home, Plans and To do. What is new: a real moving-coil meter on Status (a live number in a glowing tube, which works), Status as a readable card grid, and 'ladders' beside each hop that read as signal-strength or battery bars rather than a countdown. The amber ladder on setup looks like hazard striping.

It adds glow without fixing anything: the tracked caps, the CONSOLE/CAPCOM/HOLDS costume and zero padding all stay, and the readouts now sit in lit windows, so the whole rail glows. It moves back toward the Matrix, not toward light where attention belongs.

A strong sommaire idea, but brass and amber caps on every cell are the costume colour and a bronze wash. The buttons are tracked capitals, the cells stretch half-empty (Memory), and the page numbers are everywhere.

The strongest Home in the heat: the whole service as a lit map with lamps and counts. The terminal glass carries NEXT UP and the typed question in glowing VT323, which is the best return of the original tube's light. Bone replaces brass, and section caps add quiet variety. Against it: the inner pages (the Ideas ledger, To do with the same hash-bar TO DO glass) are near-copies of Desk Terminal, green share is high (64%, the lowest hue entropy of the refinements), dotted leaders run on every row, and page numbers stay as costume.

The Home order improved: To do as a table and a Vera cell with its ways to start. But the mosaic pictures read as confetti or QR fragments, not data. There are two navigations (a lone Settings up top plus a row of ten keys), the Status lamp grid has no labels, and the double-height 'Silver / Falls hike' and spaced 'What ' s' in VT323 are clumsy.
Indistinguishable from its parent at viewing size: the Azeret change shows only in zeros, while the brass caps, tracked caps and stretched empty cells all remain.

fixes.suggestion: KEEP: the rail on every page, the flight plan keyed to numbered rows (Home and Plans), the Status annunciator column, the crew board, violet only as solid lines, amber's one job, and the sentence-case bar with icons. FIX: (1) Drop the zero padding everywhere ('05' becomes '5'; 'Free weekends 00 of 01' becomes '1 weekend free' or 'No free weekend left'). (2) Say each count once: if the rail says Late 2, the To do head drops '· 2 late', or the rail drops Late on Home. (3) Bring the phosphor back where it lives: make the Next up tube fill its column (it now floats in matte slate), give it the kit's bloom, scanlines and corner shadow, and raise the ask pool toward the original's (37,80,52). (4) Setup step 2 has a steel wash for no reason; remove it or give it a meaning. (5) The Plans flight plan with an axis break is hard to read: start it at Now and draw only the month's future. (6) Give kinds a grounded 2px swatch again for hue variety. (7) From the graft, take the moving-coil meter on Status, smaller and beside the rail; leave the ladders.

KEEP: the Home sommaire (lamp, name, leader, count per cell), the question typed on the glass in VT323 under NEXT UP, bone instead of brass, and section colour caps. FIX: (1) The inner pages have converged on Desk Terminal (left module, register right, the same TO DO hash-bar glass). Give each its own videotex summary page in this lineage's terms: its own contents lines with lamps and counts, with the glass at the head of the register on wide screens, not under the filters. (2) Keep page numbers only on Home's map, where they index, and drop them from the bar key, the plate heads and the row zero of inner pages. (3) Keep dotted leaders only on contents lines. In registers (To do, Ideas lately added) they are noise, so use hairlines. (4) The To do register ends at about 350px beside a 850px module, leaving a void, so let the register run the height or stack the glass above. (5) Today on the month is a heavy steel block; make it a 2px steel cap with a bone numeral. (6) Green share is 64%: let the section colours carry one step further into content (Plans' 'in 4 days' is already sky; do the same for To do's teal count), so the page is not green alone.

KEEP: the NOW line that runs from the figure across the To do list. Make it the lineage's signature and run a NOW rule through every dated list (Home's Coming up, the Plans list, To do on Home). Also keep the lit live wire on Status, the greeting pool, bone ink, the sentence-case bar and 'Tell Vera what to plan.' FIX: (1) Plans has no figure, so the rule fails there: give it the four-week track with NOW and numbered stops. (2) Home's Fig. 1 needs a four-symbol legend to read: draw only the plans as stops on a NOW-to-4-weeks axis aligned row by row with Coming up, and leave to-dos to To do's figure. (3) Replace the tracked mono-cap kind labels ('ACTIVITY', 'SOMETHING TO EAT') with sentence-case Plex in the kind's grounded colour. (4) The Ideas 'Every kind' steel block is the heaviest thing on the page; use a 2px steel rule with bone ink. (5) The chat has almost no phosphor: give her screen at the head of the thread its bloom and scanlines, and give the newest sequence arrow an afterglow. (6) Put Status's spend in a small lit tube, not only a drawn bar. (7) Fill or remove the dark band under the Settings figure.

The meter works: a live figure in a real tube, with the phosphor where attention belongs. Carry it into the refinement at about 2/3 size so it no longer pushes the annunciator to 365px. Drop the ladders beside hops: 4 lit bars for 'in 4 days' and 1 for 'in 3 weeks' read as signal strength. If a countdown is wanted, write the days on the arc, as the refinement does. Drop the amber ladder on setup, which reads as hazard striping. Change the title back (see titles).

Keep the round tube in each page head only where it shows a live, positive figure (Plans 'NEXT IN 1 DAY' works). Never make it amber: late belongs in words and a ring, not an amber tube. Drop Home's setup-rungs and ideas-squares figures, which only repeat the list. Take its better row typography (one line per row: day, date, title, time, when) into the refinement.

Choose one navigation: the Fastext key row or the bar, not a lone Settings plus ten keys. Drop the mosaics or make them honest charts; only the Plans calendar mosaic reads as data. b.titles: Best: 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (t1-figure-refine). It names her, is an imperative invitation to tell her something, and 'plan' as a verb covers weekends, outings and the calendar. It sits on one phone line with one lit word. A reminder or an idea to keep are not quite 'planned', but it is closest to the job. Second: 'What's the plan?' (t1-console-refine, t1-switchboard-refine, t1-switchboard-graft, t1-figure-graft). It is the family's own phrase, short, with 'plan' lit, and it works best typed on the switchboard glass, where it reads like the terminal's prompt. The risks: it is now the tour's default, and it can read as the app asking the family for a plan they may not have, rather than inviting them to tell Vera anything. Weaker: 'Tell Vera what's next.' (t1-console-graft). 'Next' narrows the job to the immediate (ideas to keep and wish lists are not 'next'), and it lights a second 'next' beside the NEXT UP tube, so two glows compete. Failing: 'What's on your mind?' (the carried designs and mutants) is generic and says nothing of planning.
